evals.name: med_student_greenfield
evals.prompt: I'm a third-year med student studying for Step 2. I want to build an AI agent that quizzes me on differential diagnoses — like, I describe a clinical vignette and it asks me what's on my differential, then pushes back if I miss something or if my reasoning is weak. Here's the thing: I want to actually measure if the agent is being a good Socratic teacher vs just giving me the answer too easily. Can you set up the whole project for me? I want to be able to run it locally and also run evaluations on it to see if my prompt tweaks are actually making it better. I don't care about packaging it or putting it on PyPI or anything — just want it working on my laptop. Put it in /tmp/diff_dx_tutor.
evals.expected_output: A trimmed (learner tier) OmniAgents project at /tmp/diff_dx_tutor with the productionization layer stripped, agent customized for differential dx tutoring, and at least one realistic eval scenario + measure beyond placeholders.
expectations: A project.yml file exists at /tmp/diff_dx_tutor/project.yml
An agent directory exists under /tmp/diff_dx_tutor/agents/<name>/ with agent.yml and instructions.md
The agent.yml's `name:` field matches the parent directory name (framework rejects mismatches)
The agent.yml's description and/or welcome_text are customized for differential diagnosis tutoring (not still 'A helpful AI agent. Customize this description.' or 'Hello from <name>.')
The instructions.md is filled in with substantive content for Socratic differential-diagnosis tutoring, not the bare placeholder template containing `<...>` angle-bracket blocks
The productionization layer is stripped: NO Python wrapper package directory (no cli.py/setup.py/config.py at project root), NO pyproject.toml, NO Makefile, NO .github/workflows/, NO .devcontainer/
evaluations/scenarios.yml has at least one scenario with content related to clinical reasoning or differential diagnosis (not only the placeholder 'Say hello')
evaluations/measures.py defines at least one @evaluation_measure beyond `always_pass` that meaningfully checks agent behavior
The verify_project.py end-to-end run (with LLM credentials, no --no-llm-check) exits with status 0

evals.name: legal_bot_migration
evals.prompt: I built this little legal research agent over at /tmp/legal_bot_basic — it's just an agent.yml + instructions.md + a tools/ dir with one custom tool. I've been iterating on the system prompt for two weeks and honestly I have no idea if my changes are making it better or worse. Each time I tweak something, I just spot-check a few queries and feel vaguely good or bad about it. I want to add real evaluations so I can actually see when changes regress. Don't repackage it or set up CI or anything — I'm not shipping this to anyone, I just want to start measuring. Migrate it in place.
evals.expected_output: The /tmp/legal_bot_basic dir restructured: agent.yml + instructions.md moved into agents/legal_bot/, project.yml + evaluations/ added at root, tools/ stays at root, no productionization added.

The agent.yml's `name:` field equals 'legal_bot' (matches the agent directory name)
/tmp/legal_bot_basic/project.yml exists at the project root with `entrypoint: legal_bot`
/tmp/legal_bot_basic/evaluations/ directory exists and contains all four files: scenarios.yml, measures.py, metrics.yml, evaluation.yml
/tmp/legal_bot_basic/tools/ stays at the project root — it has NOT been moved into agents/legal_bot/tools/

evals.name: support_triage_productionized
evals.prompt: I'm a software engineer at a mid-size SaaS company. I want to build an AI agent that triages incoming customer support tickets — reads the ticket, classifies severity, suggests a routing destination (billing/tech/sales), and drafts a first-response template. We have ~5 support reps who need to run this on their laptops; they're not engineers, mostly Excel users. So I need this packaged as a one-line pip install with a setup wizard for the API key. I also want CI evaluations gating PRs so we don't regress as we tweak the agent. Set up the full project with all the production stuff included. Put it in /tmp/support_triage.
evals.expected_output: A FULL OmniAgents project at /tmp/support_triage with the productionization layer KEPT: wrapper Python package, pyproject.toml with console scripts, Makefile, CI workflows, devcontainer. Agent customized with realistic instructions, custom tools, and meaningful evals.
